hypothesis: Moving the target from 5% to 7% raises EV per trade even though it lowers hit rate, because the average winner grows more than the win rate falls.
mechanism: A pump that mean-reverts usually overshoots well past 5%, so a nearer target closes winners early and leaves the fat part of the move on the table while stop risk is unchanged.

hypothesis: Cutting max hold from 24h to 12h improves EV per trade by removing trades that have stopped expressing the original signal.
mechanism: Mean reversion after a pump happens fast; beyond half a day the position is no longer expressing the pump thesis and is just carrying directional market risk with no edge.

hypothesis: Raising the pump trigger from 5% to 8% improves EV per trade because a bigger dislocation reverts further against an unchanged stop.
mechanism: A larger pump is a bigger dislocation from fair value, so expected reversion is larger relative to the same stop distance.

hypothesis: Anchoring the stop to entry instead of the pump peak reduces the variance of realised loss size without lowering win rate.
mechanism: Anchoring the stop to the pump peak makes stop distance a function of how violent the wick was rather than of the risk being taken, so identical trades end up carrying inconsistent risk.

hypothesis: Widening the stop from 3% to 5% above the peak raises win rate by surviving the retest, by more than the larger losses cost in EV.
mechanism: A pump peak is set by a wick, and the hour after it routinely retests that wick before reverting, so a stop 3% above the peak is inside ordinary noise and closes trades that the thesis says should still be open.

hypothesis: Raising the relative-volume gate from 2x to 4x improves win rate by selecting exhaustion moves over thin-book drifts.
mechanism: A pump on ordinary volume is usually one participant moving a thin book, which can keep moving against a short; a pump on heavy volume is a crowd, and crowds exhaust.

hypothesis: Moving the target from 5% to 8% raises EV per trade even though it lowers hit rate, because the average winner grows more than the win rate falls.
mechanism: A pump that mean-reverts usually overshoots well past the 5% target, so the incumbent closes winners while the move is still going and keeps only the thin front of the reversion while carrying the same stop risk.

hypothesis: Cutting max hold from 24h to 6h improves EV per trade by removing trades that have stopped expressing the original signal.
mechanism: The reversion thesis is about the hours immediately after a pump; a position still open a day later is no longer expressing it and is just carrying unhedged directional risk on an alt.

hypothesis: Extending max hold from 24h to 48h raises win rate by letting slow reversions complete, without a proportionate rise in losses.
mechanism: Some pumps take more than a day to unwind because the crowd that created them exits slowly, so a 24h timeout can close a working trade just before the move it was waiting for.

hypothesis: Removing the volume gate leaves EV per trade unchanged while roughly doubling trade count — which would show the filter is not earning its place.
mechanism: The volume gate was never itself tested — it was inherited. If relative volume does not predict reversion, the gate is discarding half the population for nothing.
